features.title: [migrated from viernes 2026-08-18] THE MUTATION-EVIDENCE INSTRUMENT ACCEPTS AN EDIT THAT IS NOT THE ONE THE CONTRACT NAMES - harden .harness/agents/reviewer.md checks 3b/3c and the /sdd-pr-loop severity match. TWO CONCRETE DEFECTS, BOTH OBSERVED 2026-08-02, BOTH LABEL-VS-EVIDENCE. (1) On E14-F08 round 1 the mutation runner carried an entry LABELLED as the contract's `InlineError` mutation while the edit it applied duplicated the tab's live region as a second role=status node. The two mutants differ in exactly the property under test, so a mutant the assertion COULD detect went red under the contract's title and certified an assertion that provably could NOT detect the real defect - a broken assertion passed review. The Reviewer recorded this as its OWN instrument failure. FIX: a mutation counts as evidence only when the applied edit is the LITERAL one the contract names, and a runner must print the applied diff so the two can be compared. (2) The ad-hoc severity classifier used to drive /sdd-pr-loop matches the literal `nit` anywhere in a comment body, so Codex finding `3699045452` (badge P2) was tagged `nit` because the word 'initial' contains it. No gate decision changed (P0/P1 are tested first and both P2 and nit are non-blocking) so this is latent, not live - but it is the same defect class, and the skill's own wording ('match P0|P1|P2|nit case-insensitively anywhere in the body, first match wins') is what licenses it. FIX: match the severity BADGE form, not a bare substring. NOTE THE SCOPE PROBLEM AND DECIDE IT EXPLICITLY: .harness/ here is an INSTALLED COPY of harness-sdd (~/repos/harness-sdd). A fix applied only to this workspace is overwritten by the next harness upgrade, so the change belongs UPSTREAM in harness-sdd and then re-installed. Do not silently patch the installed copy and call it done.

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-18] UPSTREAM NIT (harness-sdd): `_rollback_frontmatter`'s empty `except (OSError, ValueError): pass` carries no explanatory comment, and GitHub's code-quality bot flags it on EVERY repo that vendors the harness. Found on viernes-bff #47 during E99-F125 and confirmed byte-identical in `~/repos/harness-sdd/tools/tasks-lock.py` main, so it is upstream code, not authored in any child repo. THE SWALLOW IS INTENTIONAL AND CORRECT: it sits in the rollback path of a failed frontmatter write, called from an `except Exception:` block that re-raises — if rollback of one file fails, the remaining files must still be attempted and, crucially, the ORIGINAL exception must be the one that propagates. Letting the rollback's own error escape would mask the real failure with a secondary one. So the fix is a COMMENT saying that, not a code change. ⚠️ FIX IT UPSTREAM IN harness-sdd AND RE-INSTALL — do NOT edit the vendored `.harness/tools/tasks-lock.py` in a child repo, which would recreate exactly the hand-synced-body divergence E99-F117 closed and would be silently reverted by the next installer run. ⚠️ WHY IT IS WORTH DOING rather than dismissing: it is a MERGE-BLOCKING unresolved review thread in six repos every time the harness body changes, so the cost repeats on every future upgrade PR. Low value as a code change, real value as removed recurring friction. While there, sweep the file for other bare `pass` handlers and comment them the same way — the bot will find those on the next pass otherwise. ⟂ [fix riding the 2026-09-04 refactor PR: explanatory comment added to _rollback_frontmatter's intentional swallow]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-18] NO FIRST-CLASS 'APPROVED, AWAITING MERGE' STATE — so the corrected `done`-after-merge ordering has no ergonomic home, and `in-review` actively MISROUTES. Surfaced by E99-F102 part A (PR #147 round 1): the docs used to say approve -> `set-status done --evidence` -> open PR, so at `done` time the merge commit could not exist and the 'prefer the merge commit' instruction was unfollowable. A fixed the INSTRUCTION (`done` is written after the merge is observed). What it could not fix is where the feature LIVES in between. ⚠️ MEASURED ON THE SHIPPED SELECTOR, not assumed: a feature left at `in-review` is NOT inert — `next-task.mjs` returns `{outcome: selected, route: reviewer, reason: feature-actionable}`, i.e. it hands an ALREADY-APPROVED feature back to a Reviewer every session. That is the defect `next-task.mjs`'s own E99-F77 comment already names ('`in-review` routes a Reviewer at an approved slice'). The `parked` mechanism DOES hold it correctly (`outcome: blocked`, code `gated-owner`, never selected) and `set-status` refuses any transition while parked, so an unpark must precede the `done` write — also measured. So the workaround exists but costs two `apply --mutator` round-trips per feature and reports an in-flight PR INDISTINGUISHABLY from external owner blockage, which is the signal an operator most needs to tell apart. WHAT THE REAL FIX NEEDS (why it was correctly kept OUT of part A): a first-class awaiting-merge hold with its own selector/diagnostic code, touching `tools/next-task.mjs`, the diagnostics, and coverage in `test_next_task.sh`, `test_feature_park.sh` and `test_dependency_diagnostics.sh` — a lifecycle change, not a documentation one. ⚠️ `none:<why>` must REMAIN a legitimate immediate `done`: console/AWS actions and supersessions have nothing to merge. The distinction to preserve is 'nothing to merge' (fine) vs 'something that has not merged YET' (the defect). Part A states this gap explicitly in agents/orchestrator.md, docs/WORKFLOW.md and the CHANGELOG rather than papering over it.

features.title: [migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P1 — BASE-CHANGE DETECTION FAILS *OPEN* WHEN THE PRIOR ROUND'S `pr.json` IS UNREADABLE, AND THE CODE'S OWN COMMENT CLAIMS THE OPPOSITE. In the `/sdd-pr-loop` body (step 0b), the stacked-PR guard reads `prior_base_name` and `prior_base_oid` out of `round-$((round-1))/pr.json` with `jq … 2>/dev/null || echo ''`, then wraps the whole comparison in `if [ -n "$prior_base_name" ] && [ "$prior_base_name" != "$default_branch" ] && [ -n "$prior_base_oid" ]`. If that file is missing, truncated, or lacks either field, both substitutions are empty and the guard is SILENTLY SKIPPED — while the round-directory scan has already advanced the counter. A rebased parent then goes unnoticed and the child can pass review and auto-merge without the restack ancestry check that block exists to enforce. ⚠️ THE CONTRADICTION IS INSIDE THE SAME BLOCK: three lines further down sits the comment 'Fail closed on either side of the comparison being unreadable — a missing prior cache or a transient API failure must not silently bypass the detection', guarding only the CURRENT oid. The prior side does exactly what the comment forbids. ⚠️ PRESENT IN 0.68.0 — verified by reading `.claude/commands/sdd-pr-loop.md:93-95` in this repo, not inferred from the 0.63.0 install where it was found. Fix: treat an unreadable prior snapshot as fail-closed (restart from round 1, or needs-human), the same way the current-oid branch already does. Found by Codex on viernes-web#95. || ⚠️ CORROBORATED AND WIDENED BY THREE MORE REPORTS (rounds 3-4, 2026-08-19). (a) viernes-users#38: on ROUND 1 `prior_round_dir` points at a nonexistent `round-0`, so the fields are empty and the SAME condition skips both the current-base lookup and the ancestry check — the runbook's own promise that 'round 1 must validate stack ancestry too' is therefore never kept, for every stacked PR, not just after cache corruption. (b) viernes-bff#50: if `gh repo view` or the `baseRefName` query transiently fails, `default_branch` or `base_ref` come back empty and the PR is treated as OUTSIDE the stacked lane entirely — a rebased parent then goes undetected, and after the child is retargeted that stale review can authorise a materially different default-branch diff. (c) viernes-infra#46 reported the round-1 case again. Fix accordingly: fetch base and head and verify ancestry whenever no readable prior snapshot exists, and stop or retry — never skip — when either value is unreadable. ⟂ [resolved by removal: E21-F07 deleted the base-change detection step entirely (v0.70.0)]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P1 — `gh pr merge` EXITING 0 DOES NOT PROVE THE PR MERGED, SO THE LOOP CAN REPORT A LANDING THAT NEVER HAPPENED. The 'Ready to merge' section sets `merged=1` directly from the exit status of `gh pr merge … --merge --delete-branch`, then runs local cleanup and reports success. Under a MERGE QUEUE (or with auto-merge enabled on the repo) that command may instead enqueue the PR or turn auto-merge on and return 0 — `gh` 2.96.0's own help says so. A PR later rejected from the queue is then recorded as landed, its local branch is deleted, and the loop returns success. ⚠️ THIS IS THE ONE FAILURE MODE THE LOOP'S OWN DOCTRINE SAYS MUST NEVER BE REPORTED AS SUCCESS: 'a merge that auto-merge was asked to land and did not land is never reported as success.' The code does not hold that line because it never observes the merged state. Fix: after the merge call, poll `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` until MERGED is observed (or a bounded timeout elapses) before setting `merged=1` and cleaning up; on timeout, needs-human. Found by Codex on viernes-bff#50. ⟂ [absorbs E99-F144: merge-step verification = mergedAt/mergeCommit observed AND headRefOid unchanged since the reviewed round]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P2 (REPORTED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY) — A ROUND DIRECTORY'S MERE EXISTENCE IS TREATED AS THAT ROUND HAVING COMPLETED, SO AN INTERRUPTED RUN BURNS BUDGET SILENTLY. The resume scan at the top of the runbook walks `.harness/.pr-loop/<pr>/round-*/` and sets `round` to one past the highest directory found. But `mkdir -p "$round_dir"` happens BEFORE preflight, before the trigger is posted and long before any verdict — so a run that dies at a transient `gh` auth failure, or is interrupted while its background watcher is still polling, leaves a directory that the next invocation counts as a finished round. Consequences: the cached watcher result is never classified; the PR loses a round from a budget that exists to bound review cost; and repeated retries can push `round` past `max_rounds` so the loop is skipped entirely WITHOUT ever reaching a clean or needs-human verdict — the resume logic was added precisely to stop budget being silently granted, and this lets it be silently CONSUMED instead. Fix: write a completion marker at a round's terminal verdict and advance only past marked rounds (or create the directory after preflight succeeds), and reconstruct or re-classify the highest cached round rather than skipping it. Found by Codex on viernes-users#38 and viernes-bff#50 as separate findings with the same root cause. || ⚠️ CORROBORATED A THIRD TIME, AND ONCE BY DEMONSTRATION RATHER THAN REVIEW. While driving this loop on 2026-08-19 the operator evaluated viernes-bookings-calendar#63's round-3 directory WHILE ITS WATCHER WAS STILL POLLING, read zero findings from the half-written cache, and merged on that. The watcher then exited reporting findings on head. The late finding happened to be a P2 on vendored upstream text, so the outcome was unchanged — but the reasoning was wrong, and a P1 would have been merged over. That is this exact defect from the other side: nothing in the cache distinguishes 'this round finished' from 'this round is mid-flight', so both a resuming invocation AND an operator reading the directory can mistake one for the other. A completion marker fixes both readings. Codex also reported it a third time on #63 itself ('Count only completed review rounds when resuming'). ⟂ [fixed via carrier in the code-ification batch, merged #165]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P2 — WITH `auto_merge: false`, AN UNRESOLVED HUMAN THREAD IS REPORTED AS A FAILURE INSTEAD OF THE DOCUMENTED HAND-BACK. The thread-ownership gate sets `merge_ok=0` and instructs 'If `merge_ok=0`, stop here — go straight to the needs-human terminal state', which returns FAILURE. But when auto_merge is off, the loop's own contract is that finishing green-but-unmerged is a SUCCESS: 'stop after posting the all-gates-green summary and hand back to the human — resolve threads if you like, but do not merge … that hand-back COMPLETES the loop: return success. It is the one terminal state where an unmerged PR is the intended outcome.' A human comment on a thread is completely ordinary in that mode, so the common case is mislabelled a failure. ⚠️ THE ORDERING IS THE BUG: the thread gate exists to authorise a MERGE, and with auto_merge off there is no merge to authorise. Fix: branch on `auto_merge == false` and take the success hand-back BEFORE evaluating merge authorization. Found by Codex on viernes-bff#50. ⟂ [batch carrier: absorbs E99-F151 (summary ordering), E99-F152 (gh pr checks --required) — four prose corrections to sdd-pr-loop.md in one PR]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP — THE MERGE STEP NEVER RE-VERIFIES THAT THE REVIEWED HEAD IS STILL THE HEAD, SO A PUSH AFTER A CLEAN REVIEW CAN INHERIT THAT REVIEW'S VERDICT. NOT reported by Codex — hit for real while driving the loop across six repos on 2026-08-19, and worth recording because the failure is silent and the artefact looks correct afterwards. The 'Ready to merge' path re-reads CI live but takes the findings from the CACHED `round-N/blocking.json`. Nothing compares `round-N/pr.json`'s `headRefOid` against the PR's current head at merge time. So if a fix is pushed after a round came back clean — exactly what happens when a sibling PR's finding applies to this one — the stale round's 'blocking=0' authorises merging a commit NOBODY REVIEWED. Observed on viernes-bookings-api#122: reviewed `ffcb7d48`, merged `efb22dd3`. ⚠️ THE LOOP ALREADY HAS THIS DISCIPLINE FOR COMMENTS AND NOT FOR COMMITS: step 3 filters inline comments by `commit_id == headRefOid` AND `created_at >= trigger` precisely so a re-anchored stale thread cannot count — the same staleness reasoning simply is not applied to the head the merge lands. Fix: at the top of the merge path, re-read `gh pr view --json headRefOid` and require it to equal the round's reviewed head; on a mismatch demand a fresh round rather than merging, and fail closed if the current head cannot be read. ⚠️ ALSO WORTH A LINE IN THE RUNBOOK: with N PRs carrying an IDENTICAL diff, a clean gate on one is weak evidence — a P1 landed on a sibling minutes after one of them had already merged. Hold identical PRs until every review is in. || ⚠️ INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED BY CODEX TWICE, on viernes-bff#50 ('Bind the merge to the reviewed head') and viernes-web#95 ('Revalidate the reviewed head before merging') — filed here BEFORE either landed, from the live incident. ⚠️ AND THERE IS A ONE-FLAG FIX THE ORIGINAL WRITE-UP MISSED: `gh pr merge --match-head-commit SHA` exists in `gh` 2.96.0 precisely to require the expected head commit, so the merge can be bound atomically rather than by a read-then-merge comparison that still races. Prefer the flag; keep the explicit comparison as the diagnostic that explains WHY a merge was refused. ⚠️ viernes-web#95 also notes the sharper variant: the pre-merge refresh OVERWRITES the cached `pr.json` with the new head before merging, so the evidence of the head having moved is destroyed by the very step that should have caught it. ⟂ [fixed via carrier in the code-ification batch, merged #165]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P1 — THE OPENCODE pr-fixer ADAPTER NEVER RUNS `init.sh`, AND THE DEFECT IS IN THE EMITTER, NOT IN A DRIFTED FILE. `gen_oc_agent()` in `harness-install.sh` (~line 3081) emits 'read the canonical role and follow it exactly / resolve relative paths against .harness/' and stops. The Claude and Antigravity emitters both add an init-and-halt directive ('Run `.harness/init.sh` before any work and halt on failure'); OpenCode's does not, and neither does the canonical `.harness/agents/pr-fixer.md` it delegates to. So an OpenCode fixer can EDIT AND COMMIT against an invalid harness, when initialization is supposed to be a mandatory fail-fast prerequisite. ⚠️ EVERY OpenCode install has this — it is not drift, so no re-install fixes it. Reported independently on viernes-users#38 and viernes-web#95; the emitter was then read directly to confirm.

features.title: [migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P1 — CONCURRENT pr-fixerS SHARE ONE CHECKOUT AND ONE INDEX. Below the escalation round the runbook spawns one sub-agent PER blocking comment, and the Agent-tool guidance encourages launching independent agents together — but every fixer runs `git add` and `git commit` in the SAME working tree. Concurrent fixers can overwrite each other's edits to one file, contend on `.git/index.lock`, or sweep another fixer's staged changes into their own commit, so the single push at the end of the round carries missing or misattributed fixes. ⚠️ THE ONE-COMMENT-ONE-COMMIT CONTRACT IS WHAT BREAKS: pr-fixer's whole discipline is 'one comment, one fix, one commit, one return', and that is unenforceable while they interleave in a shared index. Fix: state that fixers run SEQUENTIALLY, or give each an isolated worktree+branch (the harness already has `tools/fix-worktree.sh` and an `isolation: worktree` concept to build on). Found on viernes-users#38. ⟂ [absorbs E99-F147: checkout discipline first (verify/worktree the PR head), then per-fixer isolation or serialization]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P1 — THE LOOP NEVER CHECKS OUT THE PR IT IS FIXING, SO FIX COMMITS AND `git push` CAN LAND ON AN UNRELATED BRANCH. The runbook takes a PR NUMBER from `$ARGUMENTS` and, when that is absent, resolves the current branch's PR — but when a number IS given it never verifies that the local HEAD is that PR's head. It then reviews the remote PR, and the fixer rounds `git add`/`git commit`/`git push` in whatever checkout the operator happened to be sitting in. ⚠️ THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND DOUBLE-SIDED: the reviewed PR is left unchanged (its findings look unfixed and the round appears to stall or exhaust its budget), while an unrelated feature branch quietly receives commits attributed to someone else's review. Fix: before any fixer runs, check out the selected PR's head — or fail unless local HEAD equals its `headRefOid` — or run the fixers in an isolated worktree tied to the verified head. Reported independently on viernes-users#38 and viernes-bff#50. ⟂ [fixed via carrier in the code-ification batch, merged #165]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P2 (REPORTED THREE TIMES) — STACK-GUARD EXIT 6 HAS TWO CONTRADICTORY TERMINAL STATES IN THE SAME DOCUMENT. When `pr-stack-guard.sh` returns 6 because a parent PR is still open, the `guard_deferred` branch says to report it and 'exit gracefully without needs-human; the child retries after the parent lands'. The merge-order instructions above it and the Needs-human section below it both classify exit 6 as a needs-human FAILURE. ⚠️ EXIT 6 IS THE NORMAL WAITING STATE OF A HEALTHY STACK, not an error, so the needs-human reading escalates every well-formed stacked child before its parent lands. And because the deferred branch only prints and leaves `merged=0` without an explicit return, an `auto_merge: true` run can also fall through and report SUCCESS while nothing merged. Pick one behaviour — a real deferred/retryable terminal state — and make all three places agree. Found on viernes-users#38, viernes-bff#50 and viernes-web#95. ⟂ [resolved by removal: E21-F07 deleted stack-guard exit 6 and both its terminal states (v0.70.0)]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P2 — SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION READS THE WHOLE ISSUE-COMMENT STREAM, SO A STALE OR HUMAN COMMENT CAN BLOCK A ROUND. Step 3 walks `review-comments.json` + `reviews[*].body` + `issue-comments.json` looking for severity tags, but the freshness rule (`commit_id == headRefOid` AND `created_at >= trigger`) is applied ONLY to the inline comments. `issue-comments.json` is the entire issue stream, so an older Codex review — or a HUMAN comment that merely mentions 'P1' — is classified into the current round. ⚠️ IT THEN BLOCKS, AND IT CANNOT BE FIXED: such an entry has no `path`/`line`, which is exactly what pr-fixer needs, so the round stalls or burns budget on something no fixer can act on. Fix: filter EVERY source by the two Codex identities and the trigger timestamp before classifying, not just the inline stream. Found on viernes-bff#50. ⟂ [fix riding the 2026-09-04 refactor PR: classification code-ified as `wait-for-codex.sh classify` with the freshness rule applied to ALL streams, issue comments included]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P1 — AN EXHAUSTED CACHED ROUND BUDGET FALLS THROUGH TO THE MERGE FLOW WITH NO GATE VERDICT AT ALL. If a previous invocation created the CAP round's directory and then stopped or was interrupted, the resume scan sets `round` to `max_rounds + 1`. The `while [ "$round" -le "$max_rounds" ]` body is therefore never entered: no review is triggered, `pr-gate.sh` is never consulted, and no verdict exists — and execution proceeds to the ready-to-merge flow anyway. With the default `auto_merge: true`, a PR whose cap round was incomplete OR STILL HAD BLOCKING FINDINGS can be merged, provided it has no unresolved threads. ⚠️ THIS IS THE ROUND-CAP FAILING OPEN: the cap exists to force a needs-human hand-off, and this path skips straight past it to a merge. Closely related to F142 (a round directory's existence is treated as completion) — same cache-trust root, but this one ends in an unreviewed MERGE rather than a lost round. Fix: route `round > max_rounds` directly to the needs-human terminal state instead of falling through. Found on viernes-web#95. ⟂ [absorbs E99-F142: fix = a round counts only when its verdict artifact exists, not when its directory does]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P2 — THE 'all gates green ✅' COMMENT IS POSTED BEFORE THE GATES THAT CAN STILL FAIL. The Ready-to-merge section posts the success summary first, and only afterwards enumerates review threads, resolves them, runs the stacked-PR merge-order guard, and calls `gh pr merge`. Any of those can route to needs-human or fail, leaving a PR carrying a contradictory 'all gates green' comment immediately above its failure hand-off — misleading a human skimming the thread, and any automation watching comments. Fix: BUILD the summary there (it is needed for both terminal states) but POST it only after a merge actually lands, or after the intentional `auto_merge: false` hand-back. Found on viernes-users#38. ⟂ [fixed via carrier in the code-ification batch, merged #165]

[migrated from viernes 2026-08-19] PR-LOOP P2 — THE 'required checks' GATE CANNOT BE IMPLEMENTED FROM `statusCheckRollup`, AND `gh` ALREADY SHIPS THE RIGHT QUERY. Step 6 says to check 'CI green (`statusCheckRollup[*].conclusion == "SUCCESS"` for required checks)', but the rollup does not mark which entries are REQUIRED. So the instruction cannot do what it says: an optional check that fails or hangs — a nightly, an advisory scanner, a flaky integration job — stalls or hands off a PR whose required checks are all green. `gh pr checks --required` ('Only show checks that are required', `gh` 2.96.0) answers the actual question, with its own watch/exit semantics. ⚠️ OBSERVED IN PRACTICE on the viernes rollout: PRs routinely carried a pending `mutation` or advisory check while every required gate was green. Found on viernes-bff#50. ⟂ [fixed via carrier in the code-ification batch, merged #165]
